_comment: The flash-time offset checks. flashtool's -s/--status probe (connect_btl(), skip send/verify/finish) lets flash_katapult refuse a mismatched write before -f is ever called - see _verify_offset_before_write. _report_offset_mismatch is the second line of defence, checking again from what -f itself reported, for the board changing between the probe and the write; by the time that one runs the write has already happened, so it can only report, never refuse. The probe is not free of side effects: it shares -f's connect_btl() handshake, which transitions a running application into the bootloader, and -s has no finish step to jump it back - so a probed board is left in katapult, under a different by-id path over USB. _verify_offset_before_write therefore returns the device to write to, and every refusal says where the board was left.

mutations.name: the pre-write probe is wired into the write path

mutations._comment: The 2026-09-05 hardware failure. -s shares -f's handshake, which includes the app-to-bootloader transition, and has no finish step to jump back - so a board running Klipper is left in katapult under a different by-id path. Writing to the path the probe was handed is writing to a symlink that no longer exists.
mutations.name: the write follows the board to wherever the probe left it

mutations._comment: Decided from flashtool's own words, not from what is on the bus now: udev creates the bootloader's by-id symlink after the probe returns, and the dead Klipper one can still be present alongside it, so a bus reading here is a race.
mutations.name: a probe that rebooted the board is recognised as having rebooted it

mutations._comment: The re-resolve insists on katapult state rather than taking the first sighting - the stale Klipper symlink can outlive the reboot by a moment, and accepting it reintroduces the original bug with extra steps.
mutations.name: the re-resolved device must actually be in its bootloader
mutations.find: if dev is not None and state_for_firmware(dev.fw) == STATE_KATAPULT:

mutations._comment: Falling back to the caller's path when the board never reappears IS the original bug. It must raise - and say the board is in its bootloader, or a timeout after a reboot nobody asked for reads as a brick.
mutations.name: a board that never reappears refuses, and says where it is

mutations._comment: The reconnect is the flakiest step in the sequence and it happens after the reboot, so a non-zero probe exit is the failure most likely to be misread as a dead board. That is why `moved` is computed above the exit-code check rather than below it.
mutations.name: a probe that failed after rebooting the board still says where it is

mutations._comment: The CAN path is immune to the stale-path half of the bug - -i <iface> -u <uuid> addresses the board either way - but not to the reboot half: refusing there leaves a native node in katapult exactly as it does over USB.
mutations.name: a CAN refusal says the probe left the node in katapult too

mutations._comment: The build-time half. Without a recorded app_address there is nothing to compare a probe or a handshake against, so this guard is what makes either check possible at all rather than something that would always read as 'nothing to compare'.

mutations._comment: force overriding a genuine mismatch is a deliberate, single-device decision. Letting it leak into a whole-type or update-all batch would let one board's exception silently force every board in the batch past a check that exists specifically to stop a fleet-wide brick.
mutations.name: a whole-type or update-all batch never carries force, only a single device does
